name: Martinique
peoples: Kalinago communities and earlier Indigenous societies
summary: Three British occupations punctuate a long French colonial history.
notes: The chart tracks external administration, not changes between French regimes. Departmental status in 1946 and the later territorial collectivity are internal French constitutional changes.

events.title: A recorded European encounter
events.detail: Columbus reached Martinique; Spain did not establish a colony.
events.uncertainty: Sources disagree about early sightings; 1502 is a conventional encounter date.

events.title: French settlement at Saint-Pierre
events.detail: D’Esnambuc’s colonists established a foothold and expanded at Indigenous expense.

events.title: Kalinago dispossession
events.detail: French colonial expansion drove remaining Kalinago communities from much of the island.

events.title: The first British occupation
events.detail: Britain captured the island in the Seven Years’ War.

events.title: The Treaty of Paris restores France
events.detail: Britain returned Martinique under the peace settlement.

events.title: Britain returns
events.detail: British forces took Martinique during the French Revolutionary Wars.

events.title: Amiens restores French administration
events.detail: The peace briefly ended the British occupation.

events.title: A third British occupation
events.detail: British forces captured the colony in the Napoleonic Wars.

events.title: French administration restored
events.detail: The Treaty of Paris returned the island to France.

events.title: An overseas department
events.detail: Martinique became a department of the French Republic.
